heroHeadline: Day 69: Rubio Says US Expects Iran Response 'Today' on Peace Deal; US-Iran Trade Fire in Hormuz; Court Strikes Down 10% Tariffs
heroSubtitle: On May 8, 2026 (Day 69 of the US-Iran war), Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters in Rome that the United States expected Iran's formal response 'today' to a one-page Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to end the conflict — the terms include a 12-15 year nuclear enrichment moratorium, Iran handing over its 440 kg stockpile of uranium enriched to 60%, mutual lifting of all Hormuz strait restrictions, US sanctions relief, and release of frozen assets, followed by a 30-day detailed negotiation window. Iran's Foreign Ministry said it had 'not yet reached a conclusion,' while Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf mocked the process as 'Operation Trust Me Bro failed.' The peace talks came under immediate pressure after US Navy destroyers and Iran traded fire in the Strait of Hormuz — Trump dismissed the exchange as 'just a love tap' but warned Iran would face 'one big glow' if no deal was reached; the ceasefire held despite the exchange, with 22,500 mariners still trapped on 1,550+ vessels and 31 tankers (~53M barrels) blocked. Brent crude surged back to ~$103–109/bbl on the military exchange news. In a second major tariff defeat of 2026, the Court of International Trade struck down Trump's 10% global tariffs (Section 122, Trade Act of 1974) as 'invalid' and 'not authorized by law' — the administration vowed to appeal while new Section 301 investigations provide backup tariff authority. Republican base support has eroded to 68% approval (down from 95% at inauguration). Kevin Warsh's Senate floor confirmation vote as Fed Chairman and the $72B ICE/CBP reconciliation bill are both set for the week of May 11.
